convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I'm practicing what I would say if I ever saw my family again. I haven't told anyone."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
You walk to the trap line with Ofori. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Thank you. I needed someone to know, and now someone does. Please keep it there."
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"We went over this," Ofori says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod. "Okay."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What got you through the first week? The very first days."
"Shock's underrated. It's the body's way of buying you time."
"Honestly? I don't think anything got me through. I just didn't stop. Some mornings that's the whole story — you keep not-stopping until not-stopping feels like a plan."
"Still on what got you through the first week."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"I'll keep it to myself. What's on your mind?"
"Have you heard what they're calling Chorus Line? I'm pushing 'Big Ugly'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I'm staying out of the naming fight. For now. Someone always gets precious about their pick."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Rest when you can. We'll talk again soon."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."
"I sleep in shifts now — two hours, up, listen, two more. My body learned it before my head agreed. Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia never taught me that. The treeline did."
"Still on how you slept."
"I can't. Not today. Ask me when the work's done."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"The whole fire was arguing about Chorus Line last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Ugly Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 5 days back. 'Rest when you can. We'll talk again soon.' , friend."

"Still on what's been happening."

"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Right — go on, I'm listening. No pressure, though."
"Last time things were different. They always are." "I dreamed Jian was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."

"Sure. I'll be around."

"You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Quirino?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
They let the words sit there, unanswered.

"It's my uncle, Quirino. Was taken. He could fix anything. Anything. I wonder what they even measure. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"It's nothing, really. What were you saying?"
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
A wall comes down, then — surprisingly — a door opens behind it. "I wasn't a midwife. I was a truck driver. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others." Quiet. Real.

"Yeah. Sorry. It's -- never mind. Forget I said anything." They look away, embarrassed at having wanted something.
"Still on that taken person."
"Alright — I should get back to it."

lines: d39: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Jian Shao is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d39: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d39: 🕯️ Jian is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d39: Stonebridge watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.
d39: 🕯️ Jian Shao is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d39: What Jian kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d39: "Jian's gone." Ofori looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Jian." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d39: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Marco blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d39: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
d39: 📖 LEARNED: Boiling Water (Level 1). Rolling boil for 1 minute kills most pathogens. The simplest safe water.
d39: 📖 LEARNED: Field Dressing (Level 1). Break down game fast and clean. Less waste, more meat, usable parts.
d39: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d39: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Jian Shao, 39 days. The mantle passes to Marco Quezada.
d39: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Marco Quezada, 30 — a line cook. His hands know different work now: Green Whisper, Green Thumb, Literally, Rain Dancer, Cornucopia.
d39: ◈ The System updates its file: the new bearer <redacted> "Gardener of the Living Garden." It had a word for this one before the Codex came.
d39: The village's quarrel was with Jian — and Jian is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d39: At the grave, Heinrich, Ofori, Nina and 2 more speak for Marco — "Jian trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d39: The fire knew Marco before the Codex did — his name already carried weight here.

d65: 🕯️ Marco's funeral feast: 1,500 kcal from the pantry, and every shaken fire is fed — Stonebridge. The village mourns together, and the links hold because the dead are honored, not because the grief was forgotten. (Trust mended — the -8 bought back with grain.)

d65: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d65: 📖 LEARNED: Engines (Level 1). Air, fuel, spark. Every dead engine is missing one of the three — diagnose in that order.
d65: 📖 LEARNED: Repair & Mending (Level 1). Look at what's broken before you touch it: find the failure point, not the symptom. Most breaks are one small thing.
